newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMI to publish EMU convergence report Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: EMI to publish EMU convergence report Wednesday.

text.p: The European Monetary Institute said on Tuesday it would publish a report on the progress European Union countries have made toward currency union at 1130 GMT on Wednesday.
The EMI, whose decision-making council comprises European Union central bank governors and its current president, Alexandre Lamfalussy, is the forerunner for the future European Central Bank.

The institute is responsible for assessing convergence in the EU until the planned launch of the Euro in January 1999 and for helping to set up the conditions necessary for a single monetary policy. In its last convergence report, released in November 1995, the EMI said that EU states' progress toward fulfilling convergence criteria was "insufficient" and that progress on public finances in particular was unsatisfactory.
The EMI's 1996 report will be submitted to the EU Council along with a report by the European Commission, also expected on Wednesday.
